declared.title: WOOP as a Brief Alcohol Intervention Led by Lay Coaches in College Settings
declared.foundIn: reports/choose-your-struggle/counter-evidence.md (card 12); OpenAlex search « Wittleder WOOP sham heavy drinking » (2026-11-26)

population: 86 adults (54 women) recruited on a US college campus by posters, taught WOOP (41) or a format-matched sham (45) by student lay coaches in one session

findings.text: Compared with a sham version that pictures the outcome twice instead of the obstacle, WOOP led to fewer self-reported heavy drinking days 1 and 2 months later, among those followed up

support.sentence: We found that the WOOP intervention group reported fewer heavy drinking days (≥ 5 drinks for men or ≥ 4 drinks for women, measured using the Alcohol Timeline Follow-Back Method) compared to the Sham group at the 1-month and 2-month follow-ups.

limits: a feasibility pilot: 86 randomized, 47 and 43 analysed at 1 and 2 months, completers only, without imputation; effect size not reported
34.5% lost to follow-up, unequal: 44% in the sham arm, 24% in the WOOP arm (p = .051)
one outcome of three: drinking days and drinks per drinking day did not differ; drinking self-reported (timeline follow-back)
no trial registration or preregistration mentioned; lay coaches not blind to arm (participants were); no screening for risky drinking
the sham pictures wish and outcome, then a second best outcome, with the same plan format: the closest test of WOOP against only dreaming
full text read (publisher's version, open in KOPS, University of Konstanz); no sample from the Middle East or North Africa known
allegiance: co-authored by Gollwitzer and Oettingen, who created WOOP and promote it
